title: Utilizing Tunable Spatial-Momentum Resolution to Understand Collective Excitations in Solids
content: Electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) in a monochromated scanning transmission electron microscope ((S)TEM) enables new insights into the behavior of phonons and plasmons at length-scales not accessible by other inelastic scattering techniques [1]. Such high spatio-spectral resolution has led the microscopy community to push in the direction of highly convergent sub-Å probes as shown in Figure 1(a). Classically, TEM has also been a powerful tool for characterizing reciprocal space symmetries given the small wavelength and parallel beams, producing diffraction patterns with better momentum resolution, more like that shown in Figure 1(b). The ability of (S)TEM to probe the dynamics of charge quasiparticles is also unique allowing for new understanding of collective excitations in solids [2]. The flexibility of (S)TEM optics in a system equipped with a monochromator and probe corrector can measure the bulk dynamic response in real-space with sub-Å resolution or in momentum-space with resolutions <10-2 Å-1 (Figure 2(a)) while maintaining meV energy resolution (Figure 2(b)), which allows for both local and non-local information to be probed in real-space
